title: Food Forest
summary: Help establish a diverse perennial landscape of herbs, berries, fruits, nuts, flowers, and habitat for pollinators.
description: The Food Forest brings together more than one hundred plant species along hillside pathways. As it matures, it is intended to provide food, learning opportunities, biodiversity, and a living example of regenerative agriculture for visitors and volunteers.
impact: Expand perennial food production and public access to edible plants
Create habitat and forage for pollinators
Demonstrate practical permaculture design in a public park
uses: Pathway materials, signs, and volunteer supplies
imageAlt: Aerial view of curved pathways and planted areas in the Food Forest

title: Three Sisters Garden
summary: Support a teaching garden where corn, beans, and squash grow together and schoolchildren take part from planting through harvest.
description: The Three Sisters Garden demonstrates the complementary relationship among corn, beans, and squash, alongside other useful and flowering plants. It also gives local students direct experience with soil preparation, planting, watering, harvesting, and food preparation.
impact: Provide hands-on agricultural education for children
Share knowledge about complementary growing systems
Produce food while strengthening community participation
uses: Seeds, starts, soil amendments, and irrigation
imageAlt: Corn, beans, squash, and other produce harvested from the Three Sisters Garden

title: Hedgerow
summary: Build a productive living boundary with permaculture guilds, food plants, shelter, and habitat throughout the park.
description: The Hedgerow project is developing a network of useful plants and permaculture guilds along agricultural edges. Mature hedgerows can provide food, wind protection, habitat, and ecological connections while improving the visitor experience.
impact: Increase plant and insect diversity along field edges
Create food, shelter, and movement corridors for wildlife
Demonstrate multifunctional agricultural boundaries
uses: Trees, shrubs, perennial plants, and mulch
imageAlt: A planted hedgerow beside a farm road

title: Wildlife Enhancement
summary: Fund nesting boxes, perch poles, and bat houses that use natural predators to reduce crop damage and chemical controls.
description: Wildlife enhancement projects attract kestrels, barn owls, bats, and other beneficial species. Nest boxes, perch poles, and bat houses can support biological pest management while reducing reliance on insecticides and rodenticides.
impact: Support natural rodent and insect control
Provide nesting and roosting habitat
Reduce risks associated with chemical pest management
uses: Nest boxes, bat houses, poles, and mounting hardware
Educational signs and volunteer installation days
imageAlt: A kestrel using a nesting box at the agricultural park

title: Wetland Restoration
summary: Continue restoring Hog’s Gulch to improve water retention, riparian habitat, biodiversity, and watershed resilience.
description: Restoration work in the stream and connected wetland has widened channels, added natural features, and established native vegetation. Continued stewardship can improve wetland function, retain water, support wildlife, and create opportunities for public learning.
impact: Improve stream and wetland function
Increase water retention and watershed resilience
Re-establish native riparian vegetation and wildlife habitat
uses: Volunteer events, interpretation, and site access
imageAlt: Restoration work underway in a wetland channel

title: Compost & Biochar
summary: Turn woody and organic material into soil amendments that retain water and nutrients and support soil life.
description: The Compost and Biochar project demonstrates ways to improve soil using organic material generated on or near the site. Biochar is porous and stable, helping soil retain moisture and nutrients while providing habitat for beneficial microbes.
impact: Improve soil structure, moisture retention, and nutrient cycling
Make productive use of woody and organic debris
Demonstrate practical soil-building methods for growers
imageAlt: Biochar being handled with farm equipment

title: Invasive Plant Stewardship
summary: Equip volunteers and students to identify, remove, and learn about invasive plants across the agricultural park.
description: Volunteer-led stewardship activities help manage invasive plants while teaching local students and community members how to recognize and remove problem species. The project combines practical land care with public education.
impact: Reduce the spread of invasive plants
Protect agricultural and native plant communities
Build practical stewardship knowledge among students and volunteers
imageAlt: A group learning together at the agricultural park

title: Farm Maintenance
summary: Keep projects functioning through fencing, signage, planting, barn repairs, equipment work, installations, and cleanup.
description: Farm Maintenance provides the practical support that allows other projects to operate. Work can include fencing repairs, signage, planting, barn repairs, equipment operation, nesting-box installation, and seasonal cleanup.
impact: Keep the site safe, accessible, and functional
Extend the life of shared infrastructure and equipment
Provide rapid support to projects across the park
uses: Repair materials, fasteners, fencing, and signs
Small tools, equipment servicing, and fuel
Safety gear and volunteer work-day supplies
imageAlt: A compact loader used for maintenance work at the park

title: Shade Sail Area
summary: Improve a shaded gathering area with trees, sunflowers, turf, and ongoing care for visitors and volunteers.
description: The Shade Sail Area gives visitors and volunteers a place to rest and gather. Continued work focuses on trees, sunflowers, turf, shade infrastructure, and the ongoing maintenance needed to keep the area comfortable and welcoming.
impact: Provide shelter and comfort during hot weather
Create an accessible gathering point for events and volunteers
Improve landscaping around a heavily used visitor area
imageAlt: A large shade sail installed over a grassy area

title: Community Gardens
summary: Support shared garden space that builds food security, skills, environmental awareness, and social connection.
description: Community gardens provide seasonal growing space and a place for people to learn from one another. The garden contributes to food security, recreation, environmental awareness, community education, and positive social interaction.
impact: Increase access to land for household food production
Create social connection and peer learning
Build gardening skills and environmental awareness
uses: Shared tools, water systems, and plot infrastructure
Soil, compost, mulch, and accessibility improvements
imageAlt: Two community gardeners standing beside prepared garden plots

title: Historic Barn
summary: Help steward one of the North Okanagan’s remaining early-1900s agricultural barns and its distinctive gambrel structure.
description: The historic BX Ranch barn is a complex wood-frame building dating from the early 1900s. Its gambrel form created substantial loft space for hay and equipment, and the building remains a tangible connection to regional agricultural history.
impact: Protect a rare agricultural heritage structure
Create opportunities for interpretation and public learning
Maintain a recognizable landmark within the park
uses: Interpretive materials and controlled public access
imageAlt: Workers repairing the roof of the historic wood barn

title: Gathering Place / Outdoor Classroom
summary: A planned timber-frame outdoor classroom will provide sheltered space for school groups, workshops, and community learning.
description: The Gathering Place is planned as a dedicated, weather-protected setting for agricultural education and community events. Its timber-frame design is intended to complement the park while supporting workshops, school visits, food-system learning, and public programming.
impact: Provide a sheltered setting for year-round learning
Expand capacity for school groups, workshops, and public events
Create a visible community hub within the park
fundingNote: The public project page states that $200,000 has been committed through Electoral Area B and C Community Works Funds.
imageAlt: Looking upward through the structure of a timber-frame pavilion
